question: Ascent — ATK, 1v3 down, no spike, 1:02 left. You are the last attacker alive on an SMG, advancing through A Main / A Lobby with two abilities up. How do you play the 1v3?

options.label: Slow it down: use the clock, hold a tight off-angle in A Lobby and force them to come clear you one at a time
options.explication_courte: In a 1vX with time on the clock, the map is your ally — an isolated angle turns a 1v3 into three separate 1v1s you take on your terms. Your SMG wins close and you only ever fight one crosshair at a time.

sources_option.citation: In clutches, isolate the fight to one enemy at a time by holding an off-angle rather than exposing yourself to multiple crosshairs

options.label: Rush A Main aggressively to catch them mid-rotate before they group up
options.explication_courte: Dry-rushing three full-buys with an SMG hands them the numbers duel they want — you run into a stacked A and eat crossfire. Aggression only works if you can guarantee isolation, and open A Main can't.

sources_option.citation: On an under-gunned round, avoid running into grouped full-buys in the open; force isolated close-range fights where the SMG is even

options.label: Play purely for time and information, ready to disengage and save your SMG if the fight isn't isolated
options.explication_courte: Trading the round for economy is a real option down 1v3 on a partial buy — but you still have ~1:00 and two abilities, so pure saving leaves free-fight equity on the table before you've even tried to isolate one.

sources_option.citation: When a round is likely lost, preserving your weapon for the next buy can be worth more than a low-odds fight

options.label: Wide-swing the first open angle to start trading immediately and get value
options.explication_courte: Wide-swinging blind into a 3-stack is the fastest way to die for nothing — you show yourself to every angle at once and lose the one lever (isolation) that makes a 1v3 winnable at all.

sources_option.citation: Wide-swinging into unknown numbers exposes you to every held angle simultaneously; jiggle or hold instead until you can isolate

explication_longue: A 1v3 with a minute on the clock is not a shootout to be rushed — it is a sequencing problem. The three defenders have to come dig you out, and every meter of open ground they cross is a chance to make them do it alone. Holding a tight, unexpected off-angle in A Lobby forces exactly that: they can only funnel one crosshair at a time onto you, so a 1v3 decomposes into three separate 1v1s where your SMG's close-range fire rate is genuinely even or favoured. Rushing A Main instead runs you straight into whatever stack is set up on site, and three full-buys will trade you the instant you show. Pure saving is defensible on a partial buy — economy is round equity too — but with a full minute and two abilities you haven't yet tried the highest-value line, which is to isolate one fight and then reassess. Wide-swinging the first angle is the worst of all: it throws away isolation, the single thing that makes a 1v3 winnable, in exchange for a coinflip you usually lose. Use the clock, pick your angle, take them one at a time.

sources.citation: Under-gunned rounds are won by isolation and patience, not by rushing grouped full-buys into the open
